learningObjective: Describe how a custom operator is registered into a runtime so that both the compiler and the executor recognize it, and what obligations the author takes on.

softwareContext.framework: generic (ONNX Runtime custom op, TensorRT plugin, torch custom op)

stem: When you add a custom operator to a runtime such as ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, or PyTorch, which combination best describes the author's responsibilities?

options.text: Only register a Python function of the same name; the runtime automatically infers the op schema from its Python signature and generates GPU kernels for all supported dtypes by tracing example inputs at first call.
Only implement the CUDA kernel; runtime frameworks introspect the .cu source to derive the op schema, differentiate the kernel symbolically, and register it into every backend transparently.
Ship the model with the op's PyTorch source; the compiler recompiles the source on every process start to derive schema, kernels, and backward pass, so no explicit registration is needed.

Provide (i) an op schema/signature so the compiler can type- and shape-check calls, (ii) a kernel implementation for each supported device/dtype registered into the runtime, and (iii) — if the op appears inside an autograd graph — a backward or functional counterpart. The runtime performs no automatic differentiation or shape inference for unknown ops.

explanation: Custom operators require: (1) a schema describing inputs/outputs/types/attributes so the compiler and shape inference can reason about them; (2) at least one kernel per (device, dtype) combination to be supported, registered into the runtime; and (3) if used in autograd, either a differentiable formulation via primitive ops or a manual backward. None of the automated behaviors in A/B/D are how mainstream runtimes work.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: schemas are declared, not inferred; kernels are not auto-generated from a Python function.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: no framework introspects .cu source to derive schema and backward.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: shipping source and recompiling on every start is neither typical nor what enables custom ops.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: reflects ONNX custom op API, TensorRT plugin API, and torch's custom op registration.

assumptions: The runtime supports pluggable custom ops (ONNX RT, TRT, PyTorch).
nonImplications: Does not imply the author must implement all dtypes; only those declared as supported by the registration.
Does not imply autograd is always required; inference-only custom ops need no backward.
